response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB * 1.0 / NULLIF(HCT, 0)) AS ratio, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING AVG(HGB * 1.0 / NULLIF(HCT, 0)) IS NOT NULL), a AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM p) SELECT AVG(p.avg_pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(p.ratio) AS mean_ratio, AVG(p.ratio - a.avg_ratio) AS mean_excess FROM p CROSS JOIN a WHERE p.ratio > a.avg_ratio

assumptions.assumption: A patient's ratio is the average of the per-record HGB/HCT values, using only records where both HGB and HCT are non-null (and HCT is non-zero). Patients with no such record are excluded.
The cross-patient average is the unweighted mean of the per-patient ratios, so each patient counts once regardless of how many lab records they have.
A patient's average PIC is taken over all of their lab records with a non-null PIC, not only those records used for the ratio.

alternatives.interpretation: A patient's ratio is the ratio of their averages, AVG(HGB)/AVG(HCT), computed over records where both values are present.
alternatives.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID HAVING AVG(HCT) <> 0), a AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM p) SELECT AVG(p.avg_pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(p.ratio) AS mean_ratio, AVG(p.ratio - a.avg_ratio) AS mean_excess FROM p CROSS JOIN a WHERE p.ratio > a.avg_ratio
